title: Process profile
description: A declared manufacturing process capability: the rules a part must satisfy to be makeable by ONE process + material + machine combination. Profiles are DATA, authored by the user, never inferred from geometry and never invented by a tool. Every rule carries provenance because an unprovenanced number is an unverifiable claim. See docs/DECISION-LOG.md 2026-10-11: the tool may only EXCLUDE (produce a witness) - it never ranks, scores or recommends.

id.description: Stable identifier, e.g. "fdm-pla-0.4". Recorded in every run so a verdict is interpretable later.

process.description: The process family. Determines which rules are applicable at all - e.g. overhang is meaningless for powder-bed and for machining, draft is mandatory only for molding.

machine.description: Free text; the machine is what a calibrated number is calibrated TO.

provenance.description: Where this number comes from. `assumed` is allowed and must stay legible: an assumption is a finding, not a licence.

ref.description: Vendor doc, standard clause, literature citation, or the coupon/run id for `measured`.

date.description: ISO date; required in spirit for `measured` (numbers decay).

rule.description: One named rule. Rules are NAMED, not expressions: a named rule is enumerable, testable and answers "which rule judged this?". Anything needing arbitrary logic belongs in run_python, not here.

applies.description: false = this rule does not govern this process. It must still be REPORTED (with `reason`), never silently dropped: telling an SLS part its overhang needs support is wrong, not conservative.

decidable.description: Whether a tool can decide it from the mesh alone. `geometry` = evaluable now. `declared-requirement` = needs a requirement declared elsewhere (e.g. a tolerance requirement to compare against tolerance capability). `not-decidable` = cost, lead time, yield - not geometric facts at all. The rule report's unevaluable list is DERIVED from this field, so it cannot drift out of sync.

value.description: Threshold. Lengths in mm, angles in degrees (repo-wide convention: mm, z-up).

direction.description: `min` = the measured quantity must be >= value (wall, feature, gap, draft, passage). `max` = must be <= value (overhang angle, bridge span, hole aspect).

reason.description: Required when applies=false: why this rule does not govern this process.

rules.description: The named rule set. Omitted rules are treated as `decidable: geometry, applies: true` with NO value = unevaluable, and are reported as such - a missing number is never read as "no constraint".

wallMinMm.description: Thinnest wall the process can produce reliably (two free surfaces, roughly parallel).

featureMinMm.description: Smallest POSITIVE feature (pin, rib, boss). Distinct from a wall: it is bounded by one free surface, not two.

gapMinMm.description: Smallest NEGATIVE clearance that stays open instead of fusing, sagging shut or trapping powder.

overhangDeg.description: Down-facing faces steeper than this need support. applies=false for powder-bed, molding and machining.

bridgeMaxMm.description: Longest unsupported span that closes without support.

holeAspectMax.description: Depth / diameter limit for a drilled or printed hole.

draftMinDeg.description: Minimum draft for release from a mold. applies=false for additive and subtractive.

escapePassageMinMm.description: Smallest passage that lets trapped powder (SLS/MJF) or uncured resin (SLA/DLP) leave an enclosed or hollow region. applies=false elsewhere.

toolRadiusMm.description: Smallest cutter radius; internal corners below it cannot be cut and pockets narrower than it are unreachable.

tolMm.description: Achievable dimensional tolerance. A CAPABILITY, so `decidable` is declared-requirement: excluding on it needs a tolerance requirement to compare against.

surfaceRaUm.description: Achievable surface roughness. Not a geometric exclusion at all; declared-requirement at best.
